content.text:
I've put four bolder palettes on page 00 of [TaxKit — Identity](https://app.paper.design/file/01M4ADH7JQ74R04WZR9J7FXHXB/p-1-0), in a 2 × 2 block to the right of the "Stand, square" board. Each one starts from Vercel-style pure black and white and adds colour a different way. Each shows the same four things: the swatches, the hero with the lockup, a result card next to an API call, and the tax-bracket dot field.

| Palette | Colours | Character |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A · Electric | Black, white, grey and one hard blue, #0047FF | Closest to Vercel. The blue is allowed to fill whole areas, like the hero. |
| B · Signal pair | Near-black #0A0A0A, white, blue #2F5BFF for things you can act on, orange #FF6A13 for things that are live | Feels like a status page or deploy log. Orange is limited to dots and dark backgrounds, because orange text on white is too faint (2.9 : 1). |
| C · Signage | Black, white, chrome yellow #FFD400, with blue links | The boldest. Yellow fills covers and heroes, and the product itself stays black and white. Risks reading as construction or crypto if overused. |
| D · Bracket scale | Black and white, plus four colours mapped to the tax rates: sky 16%, blue 30%, violet 37%, red 45% | Colour always means a tax bracket. It shows up in charts, rate badges and the dot field, and nowhere else. |

The contrast figures on each board are calculated from the hex values.

My recommendation is A combined with D. Electric blue would be the single brand colour for heroes and primary buttons. The bracket scale would bring in more colour where it carries meaning, in the tax-rate data. That keeps the Vercel restraint in the interface and puts the colour in the data.

The manual pages 01 to 03 still use the old palette. Tell me which palette or combination you want, and I'll apply it across the file's tokens, the nine manual boards, the logo page and the six plates.

content.text:
Palette D is now applied across pages 01, 02 and 03 of [TaxKit — Identity](https://app.paper.design/file/01M4ADH7JQ74R04WZR9J7FXHXB). I checked the logo, colour, screens and in-use boards plus three of the plates in screenshots after the change. The other boards picked up the new colours through the tokens, and I didn't screenshot them.

**The palette**
- **Base:** black #000000, white, grey #F5F5F5, rules #EAEAEA, and secondary text #666666.
- **Rate colours:** sky 16% #7CC4FF, blue 30% #2F5BFF, violet 37% #8A3FFC, red 45% #FF4D2E.
- **Darker text versions:** sky and red are too faint as text on white (1.9 : 1 and 3.3 : 1). Rate labels in text use #1F6FB2 and #C8331A instead, both 5.3 : 1.
- **Amber:** stays, but only for circles and rules on construction drawings.

**The rule I applied:** colour always means a tax rate. Buttons, links, focus, the current page and the logo are now black and white.

**What changed on the boards**
- **Tokens:** "signal" is now `--color-rate-30`, and there are new tokens for the other three rates and their text versions.
- **04 Colour:** rebuilt with the new swatches, proportions, contrast table and the colour rule.
- **06 Screens:** the bracket dot field uses all four rate colours, with matching labels.
- **03 Logo family:** the lockup on a blue background is replaced by an ink-on-grey version, and the app tile is now plain white on black.
- **08 In use:** the Calculate button is black, and the social card has a four-colour bracket bar.
- **01 Contents:** the quick-start rule now reads "Colour means a rate".
- **09 Token index:** lists the new tokens.

# TaxKit

TaxKit is the public monorepo for the open-source tax engine, API, SDK and
documentation site.

The repo is early, but the main public integration surfaces now exist. The
implemented surface includes the retained standalone Bun API and a native
API/Website candidate with a take-home-pay form, accepted documentation in the same Website, an Effect HTTP API package
with health, generated docs, metadata and public calculation endpoints, a
reusable calculator orchestration package, deterministic core engine
primitives, Australian pay, income-tax and STSL rule packages, a private
TypeScript SDK package, private `@taxkit/docs-content` and
`@taxkit/docs-fumadocs` packages, shared testing helpers and shared TypeScript
config, plus private Effect-native repository release orchestration in
`@taxkit/scripts`. The SDK is implemented for local and downstream
validation, but it is not published yet.

## What exists today

- [apps/api](./apps/api/README.md): standalone Bun process that owns API
  startup, listening config and Effect runtime teardown for `/api/*`.

# Website app
`apps/web` is the native TanStack Start Website candidate. Its calculator pages use
native Effect RPC for the three supported Australian 2025–26 calculators and
all accepted documentation pages. Tax calculation stays
in the separate API app. This Website also owns the accepted documentation reader. `apps/docs` is
a retirement tombstone for the old source and dated recovery records.
## What runs where
The server has one `ManagedRuntime` in `src/lib/runtime.server.ts`. Its checked
`WebsiteServerApplication` exposes settings, the supported calculator catalogue,
calculation and five named documentation operations. The private
`TAXKIT_API` service binding supplies the server connection. Calculator calls use the native Alchemy Fetcher adapter. Documentation calls
materialise their native HTTP request with `HttpClientRequest.toWeb`, preserving
the JSON byte body and the binding's receiver. This avoids carrying a stream
owned by an earlier Cloudflare request into a later call.
The root route restores Schema-encoded settings/catalogue and seeds a React-owned Atom
registry. `calculator.atoms.ts` describes the browser connection and commands;
it creates no browser runner. Checked settings stay alive for that registry's
lifetime, including time spent waiting before the first click. The browser calls
the checked `API_PUBLIC_ORIGIN` directly at POST `/rpc`. The server function
transports settings and the checked catalogue. No calculation runs when the page loads.
Calculate sends the existing canonical request. Editing interrupts unfinished
work and keeps the previous successful answer with an out-of-date message.
